title: Your site, your rules: new AI traffic options for all customers
excerpt: For our second Content Independence Day, we’re giving website owners finer options to manage AI traffic. Instead of a one-size-fits-all block, all customers can now easily distinguish and manage Search, Agent, and Training bots, alongside the new ability to protect ad-monetized pages.
content_html:
One year ago, we declared the first Content Independence Day, and we gave website owners the means to take back control of their content. The deal between crawlers and website owners that had held up for 30 years — we crawl you, and you get referrals — was no longer true. AI was taking everything and sending back nothing, presenting an existential threat to website owners. And so we launched a one-click "Block AI Bots" option, along with a Pay-Per-Crawl marketplace.

A lot has changed in a year. Last July, conversations around “AI bots” centered around blocking AI training without compensation, pointing to the win–lose deal where content was used for model training with no value driven back to the website owner. But a desire for more nuance has emerged: Content owners still want to be able to protect their content, and they should be compensated for the original content that they work hard to create, curate, and share. We also know that locking down content isn’t a one-size-fits-all solution; website owners want more options than resorting to “block all automation, every time.”

If you run a small site, the problem isn’t just that someone could train models on your content — it's that nobody can find you in the first place. So you have to make a Faustian bargain: either show up in search and let AI train on you, or risk losing discoverability. This unfairly advantages incumbent search providers if they use the same bots for both search and training; and this unfair advantage incentivizes new players to be evasive as they try to close the competitive gap.

Now, AI can be anything

Today, AI can be in anything. Google search has changed from being sorted by AI to being a full answer engine that answers your question directly on the results page. And Google is not unique in this position — this is the direction in which “search” is moving.

We could debate the cutoff for what qualifies as “AI” today, just to find that the standard changes tomorrow. So, instead of defining a bot primarily as “AI” or not, our updated approach to classification will ask deeper questions about bot or agent behavior: What are they doing on my site? What are they storing? And how will they reshare my content?

A pragmatic taxonomy

To address these questions, we need a more nuanced view — a pragmatic taxonomy that aligns with the AI use cases our customers care about. So we are opening the discussion beyond AI training alone and focusing on three AI use cases that we want all customers to be able to manage:

  • Search: any behavior that collects or indexes your content, so it can answer questions about it later. The key is that Search is proactively building a database of your site to later respond to queries with. Site owners should expect to get referral traffic or other equitable compensation as a result.
  • Agent: automated behavior that is acting, usually in real time, on a person's behalf, to get something done right now. This includes chat fetch bots (e.g., ChatGPT-User) and browser-use agents (e.g., Gemini or Claude driving Chrome). The key is that it visits your web application in order to complete a job, and often there's a human waiting on the other end.
  • Training: a crawler taking your content to train or fine-tune a model. The key is that your data is permanently absorbed into the underlying architecture of the AI to improve its capabilities.

Many popular crawlers on the web fall into one of the classifications above; some fall into multiple. We classify plenty of other behaviors beyond the three above — including ads verification, feed fetching, and agentic transactions (more on this below). But we believe it should be simple for all website owners to manage access for these three AI-centered use cases. We believe that bot operators should separate their crawlers because that creates more transparency for website owners: allowing them to better understand why a given crawler is visiting them, as well as to better manage the access they extend to that crawler. If a company runs automation that builds Search indexes, acts as an Agent, and collects data to Train their models, then we strongly encourage that company to separate the automation into three separate crawlers.

We want a classification system that is scalable and representative of the world of automated traffic as it evolves. Tracking a bot’s purposes is nothing new, but our new taxonomy involves a few updates that better represent the state of bot traffic today. Most notably, we want to recognize that bots that have multiple purposes should be tracked with all purposes, not just one of them.

New options to manage AI traffic

We want to provide more options for managing different kinds of AI traffic, to all website owners on the Cloudflare network.

The managed preset to “Block AI bots” that we’ve announced in the past included single-purpose bots that crawled data for model training, as shown below: 

Screenshot of the existing setting to manage AI bot traffic on July 1, 2025.

But not all AI use is the same, and we want our customers to have the controls they need. So, we’re launching the ability to manage AI traffic based on three major use cases: Search, Agent, and Training crawlers. With these new options, our customers can more finely tune how they manage AI bot traffic — including customers on our Free tier.

Screenshot of the new options to manage AI bot traffic on July 1, 2026.

Setting new defaults

On September 15, 2026, we’ll be setting new defaults for each of these three classifications. For all new domains onboarding to Cloudflare, the categories of Training and Agent will be blocked by default on the pages that display ads, while Search will remain allowed by default. 

An ad is a signal that a website owner meant for a person to land there and see it — something monetizable that fuels the business. So, on those pages, we treat human attention as the end goal, and keep away the bots that may prevent this attention (i.e., Training and Agent bots). On the other hand, Search is the behavior that most naturally funnels back visitors, and we believe it’s in the interest of most site owners to allow this.

Another change that will apply on September 15 is that multi-purpose crawlers (specifically those that combine Search with Training) will be allowed/blocked according to all of their behaviors, in line with our call for transparency for website owners. Since the defaults will be enforced by the most restrictive applicable rules, multi-purpose crawlers such as Googlebot, Applebot, and BingBot will be blocked by customers who have selected to block Training (either through the new options to manage AI traffic, or through the legacy Block AI bots service).

Of course, customer choice is paramount: if a website owner wants to opt out of these new default configurations, they can easily mark this in their Security settings any time leading up to September 15, which will confirm that they want no changes on Training crawlers that also crawl for Search purposes. We’ll also continue to notify customers of the upcoming change to defaults as we approach September 15 to ensure that customers who want to choose settings different from the defaults have the opportunity to do so.

BotBase: a new visibility plane for Enterprise customers

We’re also excited to launch a major visibility update as a new feature of Enterprise Bot Management. As Cloudflare’s directory of tracked bots has grown, so has the desire to manage these bots in sensible groupings and to understand more detail about a particular bot. 

Introducing BotBase. BotBase is our new database tracking all known bots, including Verified bots and agents. This database provides a comprehensive, searchable view of our entire directory of bots, directly on the Cloudflare dashboard. We’re tackling visibility first, but, later this year, we’ll expand BotBase to provide a direct control center for known automated content on your website.

With this new view, Enterprise Bot Management customers can see the full catalogue of all Verified bots/agents and where they are classified in this updated taxonomy — a view we’ve never shown dynamically on the Cloudflare dashboard before. Customers who want to precisely target a specific bot can also easily filter for all traffic from this bot, plus copy the detection ID to use in Security rules. All of this is now live within a dedicated page, which can be accessed through the Bot Management configuration card. 

As we built BotBase, we wanted to account for all of the pieces of information that would allow us to build scalable, powerful insights from bot to bot. One of these pieces is a cornerstone for our updated taxonomy, which is based on what a bot may do on your site — its behavior. We separate these classifications as shared below, and each bot is classified with one or more of these behaviors.

Bot classification

Behaviors and uses

Search

Crawling to scan your site to help it appear in search engine results

Agent

User-directed agents visiting a page on behalf of a human

Training

Crawling to train or fine-tune models

Transact

Checkout actions on behalf of users

Data Collection

Includes price scraping, competitive intelligence gathering, and third-party analytics

Security Testing

Includes vulnerability scanning and penetration testing

SEO

SEO crawling, site auditing, accessibility checks

Ads Verification

Ad placement verification, ad fraud detection

Social / Link Preview

Link previews for social platforms and messaging apps

Feed Fetching

Includes RSS readers, podcast aggregators, and news feed bots

Monitoring & Operations

Includes uptime monitoring, webhooks, and health checks

Bold italicized rows indicate the new configurable options that are available to all customers.

How does a crawler use my content?

Another piece of information we’ve heard is important to our customers is a bot’s content use — what a bot may keep and reshare after it has crawled your content. To address this, we are building capabilities for Bot Management customers to select and block based on the “content use.” This setting can be set to one of three levels, from least to most permissive:

  • immediate — interact, but store and reuse nothing
  • reference (default) — index, excerpt, and link back
  • full — summarize and reproduce

These values can be combined with bot classifications to express nuanced rules, such as “allow all bots that are used for Search, SEO, and Ads Verification, but only up to the reference use level.” This allows website owners to make decisions in sensible groupings rather than manage individual bot-by-bot rules.

To further support this, starting today, we're testing a new signal, use, that extends Content Signals and lives in your robots.txt. This extends the three fields of the first version of Content Signals with a fourth, optional field that expresses the same preference as above:

  • use=immediate
  • use=reference
  • use=full

As with all other items listed in the robots.txt file, the values of content use signal a website owner’s preference, rather than issuing blocks directly. We’re now adding support for this extension: all customers who have already enabled managed robots.txt — which prepends the preference to robots.txt that crawling for search is okay, but that crawling for training is not — will now have the additional preference of use=reference added to their robots.txt.

# Cloudflare Managed content with original Content Signals

User-agent: *
Content-Signal: search=yes,ai-train=no
Allow: /

The contents of Cloudflare managed robots.txt with the original Content Signals values. 

# Cloudflare Managed content with the new content-use signal

User-agent: *
Content-Signal: search=yes,ai-train=no,use=reference
Allow: /

The contents of Cloudflare managed robots.txt with the added parameter.

We’re also starting to track content uses for every bot in BotBase, and when we discover a bot abusing these signals, it will lose the “Verified” status, resulting in it no longer being allowed. Today, bots that reproduce in full cannot have the Verified status.

What does it mean for a bot to be Verified?

Speaking of “Verified,” the definition of Verified is being updated to reflect the upcoming changes to default allow and block baselines. Previously, all Verified bots were allowed by default, which was reflected in our basic Bot Fight Mode offering to block unwanted automatic traffic and in our rule templates for Enterprise Bot Management customers. 

Starting today, we’re adjusting this to add nuance: non-verified bots are still default blocked, but we are no longer viewing Verified as “default allowed.” Now, the Verified label makes a bot allowable with its relevant category, meaning the allowed category (e.g., allowing Search) will determine what is allowed to access a website.

To balance this change, we’re opening up the process of becoming a Verified bot, and making it more transparent, too. To "Verify" a bot, a bot operator needs to show two things: that you represent yourself honestly, and you don't abuse the access that honesty earns. And to make this easier on bot operators, we’re currently building management tools for bot operators to better ensure they are accurately represented by Cloudflare’s classification system (to be announced in the near future). 

A preview screenshot of the upcoming platform built directly for bot operators who are part of or want to be a part of BotBase, the next generation of the Cloudflare Bots Directory.

Experimenting with transitive trust

One more piece: The bot (or agent) at your door increasingly isn't run by the company that built it. A platform like Cloudflare’s Developer Platform runs automations for thousands of different operators at once, ranging from enterprises to a developer you've never heard of. You might trust Stripe, but you don't necessarily trust everyone who wired Stripe's tools into a weekend project.

We call the case of (site owner → bot owning company → end user) a matter of transitive trust, and we're proposing to utilize the existing Forwarded header as defined in RFC 7239 that rides along with the request and allows “proxy components to disclose information lost in the proxying process.” 

This is similar to what X-Forwarded-For does for IP addresses, or X-Forwarded-Host does to preserve the original Host header. So when a website owner says, "Allow this operator," that preference will hold, whether the operator comes to you directly or through three layers of intermediaries that are trusted. More details can be found in our documentation, with a brief example to show the format below.

Forwarded: for="openai"

Adding the extension with content-use discussed above, the header addition would look something like the below, specifying how the operator says they will use the content they access:

Forwarded: for="openai";use="reference"

This also lines up the incentive model we want to foster. Losing trusted status across the more than 20% of web domains that sit behind Cloudflare is a deterrent with teeth. Trust becomes something you can carry with you, and something you can lose.

However, as bot traffic blends with human traffic, it’s possible that this system of transitive trust doesn’t carry beyond the users who can afford to be identifiable. The measures we are proposing today help to convey trust, but they won’t fit the entire web for all time. Small sources of traffic need privacy, and companies that want to preserve their own privacy commitments should be able to explore fair building blocks for the future of an agentic Internet, such as private rate limiting.

Set your terms today

These are small changes that move in the same direction: site owners get more control over who uses their content, and how. We believe the new defaults we discussed today and will soon implement are ones that encourage transparency and are more reflective of where the world is going.

Of course, the ebbs and flows of the web will continue shifting under us, and we'll keep adjusting with it. But the direction won't change, because it's the one Cloudflare started with: a web ecosystem built around trust. Where the people who make things can decide how they're used — and one where being honest about what you do earns you more access, not less.

These new options to manage AI traffic are live now, and can be configured by all existing customers in their zone Settings. Not on Cloudflare yet? Start for free to set the traffic controls that you want today.

Happy Content Independence Day.

sentences.en: But a desire for more nuance has emerged: Content owners still want to be able to protect their content, and they should be compensated for the original content that they work hard to create, curate, and share.
sentences.zh: 但更多细微差别的愿望已经出现：内容所有者仍然希望能够保护他们的内容，他们应该为他们努力创建、策划和共享的原创内容获得补偿。

sentences.en: We also know that locking down content isn’t a one-size-fits-all solution; website owners want more options than resorting to “block all automation, every time.”
sentences.zh: 我们还知道，锁定内容并不是一种万能的解决方案。网站所有者想要更多的选择，而不是诉诸“每次都阻止所有自动化”。

blocks.html_en: If you run a small site, the problem isn’t just that someone could train models on your content — it's that nobody can find you in the first place. So you have to make a Faustian bargain: either show up in search and let AI train on you, or risk losing discoverability. This unfairly advantages incumbent search providers if they use the same bots for both search and training; and this unfair advantage incentivizes new players to be evasive as they try to close the competitive gap.

sentences.en: If you run a small site, the problem isn’t just that someone could train models on your content — it's that nobody can find you in the first place.
sentences.zh: 如果您运营一个小型网站，问题不仅在于有人可以根据您的内容训练模型，还在于没有人能够首先找到您。

sentences.en: So you have to make a Faustian bargain: either show up in search and let AI train on you, or risk losing discoverability.
sentences.zh: 因此，你必须做出浮士德式的交易：要么出现在搜索中并让人工智能对你进行训练，要么冒着失去被发现性的风险。

sentences.en: This unfairly advantages incumbent search providers if they use the same bots for both search and training; and this unfair advantage incentivizes new players to be evasive as they try to close the competitive gap.
sentences.zh: 如果现有的搜索提供商使用相同的机器人进行搜索和培训，这对他们来说是不公平的优势；这种不公平的优势会促使新玩家在试图缩小竞争差距时采取回避态度。

blocks.html_en: Now, AI can be anything

sentences.en: Now, AI can be anything
sentences.zh: 现在，人工智能可以是任何东西

blocks.html_en: Today, AI can be in anything. Google search has changed from being sorted by AI to being a full answer engine that answers your question directly on the results page. And Google is not unique in this position — this is the direction in which “search” is moving.

sentences.en: Today, AI can be in anything.
sentences.zh: 如今，人工智能可以应用于任何领域。

sentences.en: Google search has changed from being sorted by AI to being a full answer engine that answers your question directly on the results page.
sentences.zh: 谷歌搜索已经从由人工智能排序变成了一个完整的答案引擎，可以直接在结果页面上回答你的问题。

sentences.en: And Google is not unique in this position — this is the direction in which “search” is moving.
sentences.zh: 谷歌在这个位置上并不是独一无二的——这就是“搜索”正在发展的方向。

blocks.html_en: We could debate the cutoff for what qualifies as “AI” today, just to find that the standard changes tomorrow. So, instead of defining a bot primarily as “AI” or not, our updated approach to classification will ask deeper questions about bot or agent behavior: What are they doing on my site? What are they storing? And how will they reshare my content?

sentences.en: We could debate the cutoff for what qualifies as “AI” today, just to find that the standard changes tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我们今天可能会争论“人工智能”的界限，结果却发现标准明天就会改变。

sentences.en: So, instead of defining a bot primarily as “AI” or not, our updated approach to classification will ask deeper questions about bot or agent behavior: What are they doing on my site?
sentences.zh: 因此，我们更新的分类方法不会主要将机器人定义为“人工智能”，而是会提出有关机器人或代理行为的更深层次问题：他们在我的网站上做什么？

sentences.en: What are they storing?

blocks.html_en: A pragmatic taxonomy

sentences.en: A pragmatic taxonomy
sentences.zh: 实用的分类法

blocks.html_en: To address these questions, we need a more nuanced view — a pragmatic taxonomy that aligns with the AI use cases our customers care about. So we are opening the discussion beyond AI training alone and focusing on three AI use cases that we want all customers to be able to manage:

sentences.en: To address these questions, we need a more nuanced view — a pragmatic taxonomy that aligns with the AI use cases our customers care about.
sentences.zh: 为了解决这些问题，我们需要一个更细致的观点——一种与客户关心的人工智能用例相一致的务实分类法。

sentences.en: So we are opening the discussion beyond AI training alone and focusing on three AI use cases that we want all customers to be able to manage:
sentences.zh: 因此，我们不仅开始讨论人工智能培训，还重点讨论我们希望所有客户都能够管理的三个人工智能用例：

blocks.html_en: • Search: any behavior that collects or indexes your content, so it can answer questions about it later. The key is that Search is proactively building a database of your site to later respond to queries with. Site owners should expect to get referral traffic or other equitable compensation as a result.

sentences.en: Search: any behavior that collects or indexes your content, so it can answer questions about it later.
sentences.zh: 搜索：任何收集或索引您的内容的行为，以便稍后可以回答有关该内容的问题。

sentences.en: The key is that Search is proactively building a database of your site to later respond to queries with.
sentences.zh: 关键是搜索会主动构建您网站的数据库，以便稍后响应查询。

sentences.en: Site owners should expect to get referral traffic or other equitable compensation as a result.
sentences.zh: 网站所有者应该期望获得推荐流量或其他公平的补偿。

blocks.html_en: • Agent: automated behavior that is acting, usually in real time, on a person's behalf, to get something done right now. This includes chat fetch bots (e.g., ChatGPT-User) and browser-use agents (e.g., Gemini or Claude driving Chrome). The key is that it visits your web application in order to complete a job, and often there's a human waiting on the other end.

sentences.en: Agent: automated behavior that is acting, usually in real time, on a person's behalf, to get something done right now.
sentences.zh: 代理：自动行为，通常代表一个人实时行动，立即完成某件事。

sentences.en: This includes chat fetch bots (e.g., ChatGPT-User) and browser-use agents (e.g., Gemini or Claude driving Chrome).
sentences.zh: 这包括聊天获取机器人（例如，ChatGPT-User）和浏览器使用代理（例如，驱动 Chrome 的 Gemini 或 Claude）。

sentences.en: The key is that it visits your web application in order to complete a job, and often there's a human waiting on the other end.
sentences.zh: 关键是它会访问您的 Web 应用程序以完成工作，并且通常有人在另一端等待。

blocks.html_en: • Training: a crawler taking your content to train or fine-tune a model. The key is that your data is permanently absorbed into the underlying architecture of the AI to improve its capabilities.

sentences.en: Training: a crawler taking your content to train or fine-tune a model.
sentences.zh: 训练：爬虫利用您的内容来训练或微调模型。

sentences.en: The key is that your data is permanently absorbed into the underlying architecture of the AI to improve its capabilities.
sentences.zh: 关键是你的数据会被永久吸收到人工智能的底层架构中，以提高其能力。

blocks.html_en: Many popular crawlers on the web fall into one of the classifications above; some fall into multiple. We classify plenty of other behaviors beyond the three above — including ads verification, feed fetching, and agentic transactions (more on this below). But we believe it should be simple for all website owners to manage access for these three AI-centered use cases. We believe that bot operators should separate their crawlers because that creates more transparency for website owners: allowing them to better understand why a given crawler is visiting them, as well as to better manage the access they extend to that crawler. If a company runs automation that builds Search indexes, acts as an Agent, and collects data to Train their models, then we strongly encourage that company to separate the automation into three separate crawlers.

sentences.en: Many popular crawlers on the web fall into one of the classifications above; some fall into multiple.
sentences.zh: 网络上许多流行的爬虫都属于上述分类之一；有些属于多重。

sentences.en: We classify plenty of other behaviors beyond the three above — including ads verification, feed fetching, and agentic transactions (more on this below).
sentences.zh: 除了上述三种行为之外，我们还对许多其他行为进行了分类，包括广告验证、提要获取和代理交易（更多内容见下文）。

sentences.en: But we believe it should be simple for all website owners to manage access for these three AI-centered use cases.
sentences.zh: 但我们认为，对于所有网站所有者来说，管理这三个以人工智能为中心的用例的访问应该很简单。

sentences.en: We believe that bot operators should separate their crawlers because that creates more transparency for website owners: allowing them to better understand why a given crawler is visiting them, as well as to better manage the access they extend to that crawler.
sentences.zh: 我们认为机器人运营商应该分离他们的爬虫，因为这为网站所有者创造了更多透明度：使他们能够更好地理解给定爬虫访问它们的原因，以及更好地管理他们扩展到该爬虫的访问权限。

sentences.en: If a company runs automation that builds Search indexes, acts as an Agent, and collects data to Train their models, then we strongly encourage that company to separate the automation into three separate crawlers.
sentences.zh: 如果一家公司运行构建搜索索引、充当代理并收集数据来训练模型的自动化，那么我们强烈鼓励该公司将自动化分为三个单独的爬虫。

blocks.html_en: We want a classification system that is scalable and representative of the world of automated traffic as it evolves. Tracking a bot’s purposes is nothing new, but our new taxonomy involves a few updates that better represent the state of bot traffic today. Most notably, we want to recognize that bots that have multiple purposes should be tracked with all purposes, not just one of them.

sentences.en: We want a classification system that is scalable and representative of the world of automated traffic as it evolves.
sentences.zh: 我们想要一个可扩展的分类系统，并且能够代表自动流量世界的发展。

sentences.en: Tracking a bot’s purposes is nothing new, but our new taxonomy involves a few updates that better represent the state of bot traffic today.
sentences.zh: 跟踪机器人的目的并不是什么新鲜事，但我们的新分类法涉及一些更新，可以更好地代表当今机器人流量的状态。

sentences.en: Most notably, we want to recognize that bots that have multiple purposes should be tracked with all purposes, not just one of them.
sentences.zh: 最值得注意的是，我们希望认识到具有多种目的的机器人应该针对所有目的进行跟踪，而不仅仅是其中之一。

blocks.html_en: Setting new defaults

sentences.en: Setting new defaults
sentences.zh: 设置新的默认值

blocks.html_en: On September 15, 2026, we’ll be setting new defaults for each of these three classifications. For all new domains onboarding to Cloudflare, the categories of Training and Agent will be blocked by default on the pages that display ads, while Search will remain allowed by default.

sentences.en: On September 15, 2026, we’ll be setting new defaults for each of these three classifications.
sentences.zh: 2026 年 9 月 15 日，我们将为这三个分类设置新的默认值。

sentences.en: For all new domains onboarding to Cloudflare, the categories of Training and Agent will be blocked by default on the pages that display ads, while Search will remain allowed by default.
sentences.zh: 对于所有加入 Cloudflare 的新域，在显示广告的页面上默认会阻止“培训”和“代理”类别，而默认情况下仍允许搜索。

blocks.html_en: An ad is a signal that a website owner meant for a person to land there and see it — something monetizable that fuels the business. So, on those pages, we treat human attention as the end goal, and keep away the bots that may prevent this attention (i.e., Training and Agent bots). On the other hand, Search is the behavior that most naturally funnels back visitors, and we believe it’s in the interest of most site owners to allow this.

sentences.en: An ad is a signal that a website owner meant for a person to land there and see it — something monetizable that fuels the business.
sentences.zh: 广告是一个信号，表明网站所有者想让人们登陆并看到它——这是一种可货币化的东西，可以推动业务发展。

sentences.en: So, on those pages, we treat human attention as the end goal, and keep away the bots that may prevent this attention (i.e., Training and Agent bots).
sentences.zh: 因此，在这些页面上，我们将人类注意力视为最终目标，并远离可能阻止这种注意力的机器人（即训练和代理机器人）。

sentences.en: On the other hand, Search is the behavior that most naturally funnels back visitors, and we believe it’s in the interest of most site owners to allow this.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，搜索是最自然地吸引回访者的行为，我们相信允许这种行为符合大多数网站所有者的利益。

blocks.html_en: Another change that will apply on September 15 is that multi-purpose crawlers (specifically those that combine Search with Training) will be allowed/blocked according to all of their behaviors, in line with our call for transparency for website owners. Since the defaults will be enforced by the most restrictive applicable rules, multi-purpose crawlers such as Googlebot, Applebot, and BingBot will be blocked by customers who have selected to block Training (either through the new options to manage AI traffic, or through the legacy Block AI bots service).

sentences.en: Another change that will apply on September 15 is that multi-purpose crawlers (specifically those that combine Search with Training) will be allowed/blocked according to all of their behaviors, in line with our call for transparency for website owners.
sentences.zh: 将于 9 月 15 日实施的另一项变更是，多功能爬虫（特别是那些将搜索与训练相结合的爬虫）将根据其所有行为进行允许/阻止，这符合我们对网站所有者透明度的呼吁。

sentences.en: Since the defaults will be enforced by the most restrictive applicable rules, multi-purpose crawlers such as Googlebot, Applebot, and BingBot will be blocked by customers who have selected to block Training (either through the new options to manage AI traffic, or through the legacy Block AI bots service).
sentences.zh: 由于默认设置将由最严格的适用规则强制执行，因此选择阻止训练的客户（通过管理 AI 流量的新选项或通过旧的阻止 AI 机器人服务）将阻止 Googlebot、Applebot 和 BingBot 等多用途爬虫。

blocks.html_en: Of course, customer choice is paramount: if a website owner wants to opt out of these new default configurations, they can easily mark this in their Security settings any time leading up to September 15, which will confirm that they want no changes on Training crawlers that also crawl for Search purposes. We’ll also continue to notify customers of the upcoming change to defaults as we approach September 15 to ensure that customers who want to choose settings different from the defaults have the opportunity to do so.

sentences.en: Of course, customer choice is paramount: if a website owner wants to opt out of these new default configurations, they can easily mark this in their Security settings any time leading up to September 15, which will confirm that they want no changes on Training crawlers that also crawl for Search purposes.
sentences.zh: 当然，客户的选择至关重要：如果网站所有者想要选择退出这些新的默认配置，他们可以在 9 月 15 日之前的任何时间轻松地在安全设置中标记这一点，这将确认他们不希望对同样为搜索目的进行爬行的训练爬网程序进行任何更改。

sentences.en: We’ll also continue to notify customers of the upcoming change to defaults as we approach September 15 to ensure that customers who want to choose settings different from the defaults have the opportunity to do so.
sentences.zh: 临近 9 月 15 日，我们还将继续通知客户即将发生的默认设置更改，以确保想要选择与默认设置不同的设置的客户有机会这样做。

blocks.html_en: We’re also excited to launch a major visibility update as a new feature of Enterprise Bot Management. As Cloudflare’s directory of tracked bots has grown, so has the desire to manage these bots in sensible groupings and to understand more detail about a particular bot.

sentences.en: As Cloudflare’s directory of tracked bots has grown, so has the desire to manage these bots in sensible groupings and to understand more detail about a particular bot.

We’re tackling visibility first, but, later this year, we’ll expand BotBase to provide a direct control center for known automated content on your website.

content_html_zh:
一年前，我们宣布了第一个内容独立日，我们为网站所有者提供了收回对其内容的控制权的方法。 爬虫和网站所有者之间持续了 30 年的协议——我们抓取你，你得到推荐——不再成立。 人工智能拿走了一切，却什么也没有发回，这对网站所有者构成了生存威胁。 因此，我们推出了一键式“阻止人工智能机器人”选项，以及按次抓取付费市场。

一年内发生了很多变化。 去年 7 月，围绕“人工智能机器人”的讨论集中在无补偿地阻止人工智能训练，这表明内容被用于模型训练，而没有价值返回给网站所有者，这是一种双赢的交易。 但更多细微差别的愿望已经出现：内容所有者仍然希望能够保护他们的内容，他们应该为他们努力创建、策划和共享的原创内容获得补偿。 我们还知道，锁定内容并不是一种万能的解决方案。网站所有者想要更多的选择，而不是诉诸“每次都阻止所有自动化”。

如果您运营一个小型网站，问题不仅在于有人可以根据您的内容训练模型，还在于没有人能够首先找到您。 因此，你必须做出浮士德式的交易：要么出现在搜索中并让人工智能对你进行训练，要么冒着失去被发现性的风险。 如果现有的搜索提供商使用相同的机器人进行搜索和培训，这对他们来说是不公平的优势；这种不公平的优势会促使新玩家在试图缩小竞争差距时采取回避态度。

现在，人工智能可以是任何东西

如今，人工智能可以应用于任何领域。 谷歌搜索已经从由人工智能排序变成了一个完整的答案引擎，可以直接在结果页面上回答你的问题。 谷歌在这个位置上并不是独一无二的——这就是“搜索”正在发展的方向。

我们今天可能会争论“人工智能”的界限，结果却发现标准明天就会改变。 因此，我们更新的分类方法不会主要将机器人定义为“人工智能”，而是会提出有关机器人或代理行为的更深层次问题：他们在我的网站上做什么？ 他们存储什么？ 他们将如何转发我的内容？

实用的分类法

为了解决这些问题，我们需要一个更细致的观点——一种与客户关心的人工智能用例相一致的务实分类法。 因此，我们不仅开始讨论人工智能培训，还重点讨论我们希望所有客户都能够管理的三个人工智能用例：

  • 搜索：任何收集或索引您的内容的行为，以便稍后可以回答有关该内容的问题。 关键是搜索会主动构建您网站的数据库，以便稍后响应查询。 网站所有者应该期望获得推荐流量或其他公平的补偿。
  • 代理：自动行为，通常代表一个人实时行动，立即完成某件事。 这包括聊天获取机器人（例如，ChatGPT-User）和浏览器使用代理（例如，驱动 Chrome 的 Gemini 或 Claude）。 关键是它会访问您的 Web 应用程序以完成工作，并且通常有人在另一端等待。
  • 训练：爬虫利用您的内容来训练或微调模型。 关键是你的数据会被永久吸收到人工智能的底层架构中，以提高其能力。

网络上许多流行的爬虫都属于上述分类之一；有些属于多重。 除了上述三种行为之外，我们还对许多其他行为进行了分类，包括广告验证、提要获取和代理交易（更多内容见下文）。 但我们认为，对于所有网站所有者来说，管理这三个以人工智能为中心的用例的访问应该很简单。 我们认为机器人运营商应该分离他们的爬虫，因为这为网站所有者创造了更多透明度：使他们能够更好地理解给定爬虫访问它们的原因，以及更好地管理他们扩展到该爬虫的访问权限。 如果一家公司运行构建搜索索引、充当代理并收集数据来训练模型的自动化，那么我们强烈鼓励该公司将自动化分为三个单独的爬虫。

我们想要一个可扩展的分类系统，并且能够代表自动流量世界的发展。 跟踪机器人的目的并不是什么新鲜事，但我们的新分类法涉及一些更新，可以更好地代表当今机器人流量的状态。 最值得注意的是，我们希望认识到具有多种目的的机器人应该针对所有目的进行跟踪，而不仅仅是其中之一。

管理人工智能流量的新选项

我们希望为 Cloudflare 网络上的所有网站所有者提供更多选项来管理不同类型的 AI 流量。

我们过去宣布的“阻止人工智能机器人”的托管预设包括抓取数据以进行模型训练的单一用途机器人，如下所示：

2025 年 7 月 1 日管理 AI 机器人流量的现有设置的屏幕截图。

但并非所有人工智能的使用都是相同的，我们希望我们的客户拥有他们需要的控制。 因此，我们推出了基于三个主要用例管理人工智能流量的功能：搜索、代理和训练爬虫。 有了这些新选项，我们的客户可以更精细地调整他们管理人工智能机器人流量的方式——包括我们免费套餐的客户。

2026 年 7 月 1 日管理 AI 机器人流量的新选项的屏幕截图。

设置新的默认值

2026 年 9 月 15 日，我们将为这三个分类设置新的默认值。 对于所有加入 Cloudflare 的新域，在显示广告的页面上默认会阻止“培训”和“代理”类别，而默认情况下仍允许搜索。

广告是一个信号，表明网站所有者想让人们登陆并看到它——这是一种可货币化的东西，可以推动业务发展。 因此，在这些页面上，我们将人类注意力视为最终目标，并远离可能阻止这种注意力的机器人（即训练和代理机器人）。 另一方面，搜索是最自然地吸引回访者的行为，我们相信允许这种行为符合大多数网站所有者的利益。

将于 9 月 15 日实施的另一项变更是，多功能爬虫（特别是那些将搜索与训练相结合的爬虫）将根据其所有行为进行允许/阻止，这符合我们对网站所有者透明度的呼吁。 由于默认设置将由最严格的适用规则强制执行，因此选择阻止训练的客户（通过管理 AI 流量的新选项或通过旧的阻止 AI 机器人服务）将阻止 Googlebot、Applebot 和 BingBot 等多用途爬虫。

当然，客户的选择至关重要：如果网站所有者想要选择退出这些新的默认配置，他们可以在 9 月 15 日之前的任何时间轻松地在安全设置中标记这一点，这将确认他们不希望对同样为搜索目的进行爬行的训练爬网程序进行任何更改。 临近 9 月 15 日，我们还将继续通知客户即将发生的默认设置更改，以确保想要选择与默认设置不同的设置的客户有机会这样做。

BotBase：面向企业客户的新可见性平面

我们还很高兴推出重大可见性更新，作为企业机器人管理的新功能。 随着 Cloudflare 跟踪的机器人程序目录的不断增长，人们对以合理的分组管理这些机器人程序并了解有关特定机器人程序的更多详细信息的愿望也越来越强烈。

介绍 BotBase。 BotBase 是我们跟踪所有已知机器人的新数据库，包括经过验证的机器人和代理。 该数据库直接在 Cloudflare 仪表板上提供了整个机器人目录的全面、可搜索的视图。 我们首先解决可见性问题，但今年晚些时候，我们将扩展 BotBase，为您网站上的已知自动化内容提供直接控制中心。

通过这个新视图，企业机器人管理客户可以查看所有已验证机器人/代理的完整目录以及它们在此更新的分类法中的分类位置 - 这是我们之前从未在 Cloudflare 仪表板上动态显示的视图。 想要精确定位特定机器人的客户还可以轻松过滤来自该机器人的所有流量，并复制检测 ID 以在安全规则中使用。 所有这些现在都位于一个专用页面中，可以通过机器人管理配置卡进行访问。

在构建 BotBase 时，我们希望考虑所有信息，以便我们能够构建可扩展的、强大的机器人洞察。 其中之一是我们更新的分类法的基石，该分类法基于机器人可能在您的网站上执行的操作（其行为）。 我们将这些分类分开，如下所示，每个机器人都根据这些行为中的一种或多种进行分类。

抓取工具如何使用我的内容？

我们听说的另一条对我们的客户很重要的信息是机器人的内容使用——机器人在抓取您的内容后可能会保留和重新共享的内容。 为了解决这个问题，我们正在为机器人管理客户构建基于“内容使用”进行选择和阻止的功能。 此设置可以设置为三个级别之一（从最宽松到最宽松）：

  • 即时 - 交互，但不存储和重用任何内容
  • 参考（默认）——索引、摘录和反向链接
  • 完整——总结和重现

这些值可以与机器人分类相结合来表达细致入微的规则，例如“允许用于搜索、SEO 和广告验证的所有机器人，但仅限于参考使用级别”。 这使得网站所有者能够在合理的分组中做出决策，而不是管理单独的机器人规则。

为了进一步支持这一点，从今天开始，我们正在测试一个新信号 use，它扩展了内容信号并存在于您的 robots.txt 中。 这用第四个可选字段扩展了内容信号第一版本的三个字段，该字段表达了与上面相同的偏好：

  • 使用=立即
  • 使用=参考
  • 使用=完整

与 robots.txt 文件中列出的所有其他项目一样，内容使用的值表示网站所有者的偏好，而不是直接发布块。 我们现在正在添加对此扩展的支持：所有已启用托管 robots.txt 的客户（在 robots.txt 前面添加可以进行搜索爬行，但不能进行训练爬行的首选项）现在将在其 robots.txt 中添加 use=reference 的额外首选项。

# Cloudflare Managed content with original Content Signals

User-agent: *
Content-Signal: search=yes,ai-train=no
Allow: /

Cloudflare 的内容使用原始内容信号值管理 robots.txt。

# Cloudflare Managed content with the new content-use signal

User-agent: *
Content-Signal: search=yes,ai-train=no,use=reference
Allow: /

Cloudflare 使用添加的参数管理 robots.txt 的内容。

我们还开始跟踪 BotBase 中每个机器人的内容使用情况，当我们发现机器人滥用这些信号时，它将失去“已验证”状态，从而不再被允许。 如今，完全复制的机器人无法具有“已验证”状态。

机器人经过验证意味着什么？

说到“已验证”，“已验证”的定义正在更新，以反映默认允许和阻止基线即将发生的变化。 以前，默认情况下允许所有经过验证的机器人，这反映在我们用于阻止不需要的自动流量的基本机器人战斗模式产品以及我们面向企业机器人管理客户的规则模板中。

从今天开始，我们对此进行了调整以添加细微差别：未经验证的机器人仍然默认被阻止，但我们不再将已验证视为“默认允许”。 现在，“已验证”标签使机器人可以使用其相关类别，这意味着允许的类别（例如，允许搜索）将决定允许哪些内容访问网站。

为了平衡这一变化，我们开放了成为经过验证的机器人的流程，并使其更加透明。 要“验证”机器人，机器人操作员需要展示两件事：您诚实地代表自己，并且您不会滥用诚实所获得的访问权限。 为了让机器人操作员更轻松地做到这一点，我们目前正在为机器人操作员构建管理工具，以更好地确保 Cloudflare 的分类系统（将在不久的将来宣布）准确地代表他们。

即将推出的平台的预览屏幕截图，该平台直接为属于或想要成为下一代 Cloudflare 机器人目录 BotBase 一部分的机器人操作员构建。

尝试传递信任

还有一点：你家门口的机器人（或代理）越来越多地不再由构建它的公司运行。 像 Cloudflare 的开发者平台这样的平台可以同时为数千个不同的运营商运行自动化，范围从企业到您从未听说过的开发人员。 您可能信任 Stripe，但您不一定信任所有将 Stripe 工具连接到周末项目中的人。

我们将（网站所有者 → 机器人拥有公司 → 最终用户）的情况称为传递信任问题，并且我们建议利用 RFC 7239 中定义的现有转发标头，该标头随请求一起运行，并允许“代理组件披露在代理过程中丢失的信息”。

这类似于 X-Forwarded-For 对 IP 地址所做的操作，或者 X-Forwarded-Host 对保留原始主机标头所做的操作。 因此，当网站所有者说“允许该运营商”时，无论该运营商直接还是通过受信任的三层中介来找您，该偏好都会保留。 更多详细信息可以在我们的文档中找到，并通过一个简短的示例来显示下面的格式。

转发：for="openai"

添加上面讨论的内容使用扩展，标头添加将如下所示，指定操作员如何使用他们访问的内容：

转发：for="openai";use="reference"

这也符合我们想要培育的激励模式。 Cloudflare 背后超过 20% 的网络域失去可信状态是一种强有力的威慑。 信任成为你可以随身携带的东西，也成为你可能失去的东西。

然而，由于机器人流量与人类流量混合在一起，这种传递信任系统可能无法超越有能力被识别的用户。 我们今天提出的措施有助于传达信任，但它们并不永远适合整个网络。 小流量来源需要隐私，想要保留自己隐私承诺的公司应该能够为代理互联网的未来探索公平的构建模块，例如私人速率限制。

今天就设定您的条件

这些都是朝同一方向发展的小变化：网站所有者可以更好地控制谁使用其内容以及如何使用。 我们相信，我们今天讨论的并将很快实施的新默认设置是鼓励透明度的，并且更能反映世界的发展方向。

当然，网络的潮起潮落将在我们的领导下继续变化，我们将不断调整。 但方向不会改变，因为这是 Cloudflare 的起点：围绕信任构建的 Web 生态系统。 制造者可以决定如何使用它们，而诚实地对待自己所做的事情可以为您赢得更多而不是更少的机会。

这些管理人工智能流量的新选项现已上线，所有现有客户都可以在其区域设置中进行配置。 还没有使用 Cloudflare 吗？ 立即开始免费设置您想要的交通控制。
